Nighttime museum visits exceed 1.3 million
Unknown
Unknown Publisher
2026-10-18
08:54:38 UTC
17:54:38 KST

The number of visitors to museums and archaeological sites in Türkiye under the nighttime museum program reached 1,326,590, a 32 percent increase compared with the same period last year, Culture and Tourism Minister Mehmet Nuri Ersoy has announced.
The program allows visitors to explore the country’s historical and cultural heritage after sunset, offering a different perspective on museums and archaeological sites.
Announcing the figures on social media, Ersoy said the program had attracted growing interest, adding that the ministry would continue working to bring cultural heritage to wider audiences and transform museums and archaeological sites into living spaces.
“We are delighted to bring the unique beauty of our history and cultural heritage together with visitors in the enchanting atmosphere of the night,” Ersoy said.
The total number of visitors rose from 1,008,080 last year to 1,326,590 this year, according to the minister.
Ephesus Archaeological Site in İzmir ranked first, welcoming 501,811 visitors, up 36 percent from 368,731 last year.
Istanbul’s iconic Galata Tower came second with 277,557 visitors, an increase of 35 percent from 205,344 a year earlier.
Hierapolis Archaeological Site in Denizli, also known as Pamukkale, ranked third with 190,910 visitors.
The Bodrum Museum of Underwater Archaeology in Muğla followed with 62,071 visitors, ahead of Didim Archaeological Site in Aydın with 60,884 and Marmaris Museum in Muğla with 50,053.
Several other museums and archaeological sites also recorded substantial growth.
Visitor numbers at the Istanbul Archaeology Museums rose from 8,789 to 24,850, an increase of 183 percent.
At Didim Archaeological Site, the figure climbed from 27,846 to 60,884, representing a 119 percent increase.
Patara Archaeological Site in Antalya welcomed 28,021 visitors, up 98 percent from 14,141 last year.
At the Terrace Houses of Ephesus in İzmir, visitor numbers increased by 82 percent, from 10,718 to 19,541.
HH Nighttime visits extended at selected sites
The 2026 nighttime museum program ran from June 1 to Oct. 1 at 22 locations affiliated with the Culture and Tourism Ministry’s General Directorate of Cultural Heritage and Museums, comprising 11 museums and 11 archaeological sites.
Following public demand, the program was extended until Oct. 15 at Ephesus and Side, while nighttime visits at Göreme Archaeological Site in Nevşehir will continue until Oct. 31.
The program at Galata Tower in Istanbul will operate throughout the year.
The ministry aims to expand access to the country’s cultural heritage by extending visiting hours at museums and archaeological sites.

Veteran Turkish artist Süleyman Saim Tekcan dies at 86
Unknown
Unknown Publisher
2026-10-18
08:54:00 UTC
17:54:00 KST

Süleyman Saim Tekcan, the acclaimed Turkish artist and printmaker honored with the 2022 Presidential Culture and Arts Grand Award, has died at the age of 86.
His family announced his death on the artist’s social media account, expressing deep sorrow over the loss of “our beloved father, the great master of Turkish art, Süleyman Saim Tekcan.”
“Devoting his life to art, education and the transmission of cultural heritage to future generations, Tekcan left behind an invaluable legacy through his unique works, the artists he trained and his lasting contributions to Turkish art history,” the family said in a statement.
It added that people who placed human values above transient ones continued to live on through their works, the people they mentored and the lives they touched.
“We bid farewell with love and respect to the great master who devoted his life to serving art and humanity,” the statement said.
Born in Trabzon on Oct. 6, 1940, Tekcan was one of the pioneering figures in Türkiye’s original printmaking tradition. Alongside his artistic career, he was also known for his work as an educator and institution founder.
He graduated from the Department of Art and Crafts at Ankara’s Gazi Education Institute in 1961. He later expanded his artistic education through research into printmaking in Germany, combining his work in painting and engraving with his academic background and making significant contributions to the development of original printmaking in Türkiye.
One of the most enduring achievements of his career was the establishment of the Istanbul Museum of Graphic Arts (IMOGA) in 2004.
Bringing together production, archiving and exhibition facilities for original prints, the museum represented an institutional continuation of the workshop tradition Tekcan had developed over the years.

Sacred sites of the Eastern Rhodopes: The Wooden Mosque near Podkova
Unknown
Unknown Publisher
2026-10-18
08:50:25 UTC
17:50:25 KST

Author
Krasimir Martinov
News
Sacred sites of the Eastern Rhodopes: The Wooden Mosque near Podkova
Sunday 18 October 2026 10:35
Sunday, 18 October 2026, 10:35
The Wooden Mosque above the village of Podkova
PHOTO Krasimir Martinov
Font size
High above the village of Podkova, in the Kardzhali region of southern Bulgaria, rises the minaret of one of the country’s oldest mosques— the Wooden Mosque, also known as the Mosque of the Seven Maidens.
This sacred place is deeply revered by the local population, made up largely of Bulgarian Muslims and ethnic Turks who follow Islam. It is also included in tourist routes showcasing the cultural and historical heritage of the Eastern Rhodopes and draws many visitors every year.
Although the year of its construction is known-1428-little else is known about the mosque’s history. Tour guides, however, are eager to tell the legend that the Wooden Mosque was built by seven young women whose loved ones never returned from war. They sold all their dowries to buy the building materials and constructed the mosque in a single night. Afterward, they were never seen again.
It is believed that this happened on 6 May, during Hıdırellez, a spring festival celebrated by Muslims. Every year on this date, people from across Bulgaria, as well as neighbouring Greece and Türkiye, gather in the mosque’s courtyard. They recite mevlid (verses praising the life and deeds of the Prophet Muhammad), read from the Quran, and offer prayers. Guests are also treated to pilaf.
Tour guide Georgi Kyuchukov
PHOTO Krasimir Martinov
“As we mentioned, this is a legend in which the seven maidens lose their fiancés”, explains our tour guide, Georgi Kyuchukov. “But if we walk a little further, right next to the mosque, you will see seven unmarked graves. They were most likely built in their honour and are linked to the story we have just told. Perhaps this suggests that the story is more than just a legend. It is something the people here believe in.”
The mosque, which is nearly 600 years old, is also remarkable for its architecture. It is said that not a single nail was used in its construction. In 2009, the mosque was restored using traditional building techniques and designated a cultural monument. The 24-metre-high wooden minaret was built in 2018.
The village cemetery is located right next to the mosque and can be reached via its beautiful courtyard. The area is dotted with stones believed to possess healing properties.
''Local people believe that the stones give energy and have the power to heal. No one knows how long these stones have been here, but people revere them as places they visit to heal their ailments. You will notice pieces of clothing tied to the surrounding trees. This is based on the belief that you must leave something of yourself behind so that your illness stays here and does not follow you back home.''
One of the most remarkable is the “Pierced Stone”, known in Turkish as “Demitlikaya.” It is believed to cure various ailments, including infertility. The only condition is that visitors pass through the hole in the stone three times in a counterclockwise direction.
''People believe that the mystical healing powers of this place are strongest on the night of 5–6 May. Passing through the stone three times in a counterclockwise direction is said to bring forgiveness for your sins. One stone is used to relieve joint pain by kneeling on it. Another is believed to heal lower back pain, and a third that is believed to cure headaches. Each stone has a sign explaining what visitors should do at that particular spot.''
If our guide’s story about the Wooden Mosque near the village of Podkova has sparked your interest and you are already making plans to visit, here is a useful tip: the village, located just 15 kilometres from the Bulgarian-Greek border, is accessible by train as well as by car.
The journey aboard the “Rhodope Caterpillar”, as locals affectionately call the diesel train that crawls along the slopes of the Eastern Rhodopes, promises a unique experience. You can catch it in Dimitrovgrad, Haskovo or Kardzhali, and it will take you to Podkova railway station, the southernmost railway station in Bulgaria.
Translated by Kostadin Atanasov
This publication was created by: Kostadin Atanasov

Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu warned that Iran was developing intercontinental ballistic missiles and pursuing nuclear weapons with the aim of threatening American cities, telling FOX News on Saturday that the US, rather than Israel, was the Iranian regime's ultimate target.
Netanyahu argued that Iran's ambitions extend beyond Israel, warning that the regime intends to target both the US and Europe if it succeeds in destroying Israel. He said Iran's development of long-range missiles and pursuit of a nuclear arsenal were intended to place American cities at the mercy of the regime.
"They understand that if they can destroy Israel, then they can conquer the Middle East, control the waterways of the world... and then proceed to the next target, which is you. That's why they're building intercontinental missiles: to reach the United States," Netanyahu said.
"This is a regime that chants death to Israel, death to America. You are the real target. And I think we are well on our way to achieving this, with President Trump's brilliant leadership, both military and, then, economic blockade."
The prime minister explained that the Iranian regime views the US as "the great Satan" and Israel as the "little Satan," before directing a remark at European countries.
He said he "hoped our European friends are not offended; you are seen as the middle-sized Satan, you are mediocre in so many ways."
"Iran would be a nuclear power as we've never seen in the entire world, because they don't have this careful calculus of cause and benefit. Because they are so fanatic. So you can't win them over, you can't buy them out," he said.
Netanyahu also described the Iranian regime as a "malevolent power" operating alongside what he called the "Three Hs": Hamas, Hezbollah, and the Houthis.
"They are the arms of this toxic octopus. And it's not Iranian people; they are great people," he added.
Eliminating the Iranian threat was the first of three priorities Netanyahu outlined for his next term if reelected in the October 27 Knesset election, alongside expanding the Abraham Accords and establishing Israel as a global leader in artificial intelligence.
"First, we will achieve the complete elimination of the Iranian threat to Israel, to America, and to the entire world," Netanyahu said.
Expanding Abraham Accords as a key objective
"Second thing is to expand the historic Abraham Accords that [US President Donald] Trump and I forged here with four Arab states," Netanyahu continued.
"There are many more that are waiting in this precise moment, because they saw our strength, our power and fortitude. And they want to join us. So let's create an axis of peace and moderation against these barbarians who shoot their own people," he said.
Netanyahu also said he plans to "forge a different future, a different Middle East, and also a different world" if reelected.
Artificial Intelligence to help humankind
Netanyahu's third priority focused on artificial intelligence, and the prime minister said he agreed with Trump on both the dangers the technology poses and its potential benefits for humanity.
"I plan to seize the future with the 'Neverland AI,' the 'super intelligence,' as the president calls it. He is absolutely right; they are dangerous, but their possibilities in health, in agriculture, in transport, and in education," he explained.
"You can personalize AI for every child; they have their own potential, and you can give them the best teachers on the planet. We are doing it today in Israel, and we intend to be the world leaders in that area too. These are all amazing things," he added.
Netanyahu also pointed to Israel's economic performance, which he described as among the strongest in the developed world.
"By the way, the economy, according to the International Monetary Fund (IMF), is leading all the Western countries, the OCD countries, with the greatest growth. That's after three years of war. I want to push that even further, bring a better future to Israel, to our neighbors, to our great ally the United States."

Herzog meets Bahrain's foreign minister in Azerbaijan as Baku emerges as a regional hub
Unknown
Unknown Publisher
2026-10-18
08:49:14 UTC
17:49:14 KST

President Isaac Herzog’s meeting with Bahraini Foreign Minister Abdullatif bin Rashid al-Zayani in Baku on Wednesday highlighted Azerbaijan’s increasingly important role in regional diplomacy. At a time when relations across the Middle East remain strained, the Azerbaijani capital has become a meeting point for countries that do not always find it easy to talk to one another.
The meeting took place on the sidelines of the Conference on Interaction and Confidence Building Measures in Asia (CICA) summit, hosted by Azerbaijan. According to Herzog’s office, the two discussed strengthening the Abraham Accords and expanding regional cooperation. Herzog also met Azerbaijani President Ilham Aliyev to discuss bilateral relations and regional security.
For Azerbaijan, an emerging middle power, the meetings reflect a diplomatic role that has developed over the years. The country maintains close relations with Israel while preserving strong ties with Turkey, Bahrain, the United Arab Emirates and other Muslim-majority countries. Its ability to work with governments whose interests sometimes conflict has made it a useful venue for sensitive discussions.
Azerbaijan’s diplomatic role allows for ‘reconciliation without a public stage’
Joseph Epstein, director of the Turan Research Center and a senior fellow at the Yorktown Institute, describes this approach as “reconciliation without a public stage.”
“Azerbaijan established relations with Israel in 1992 and has kept them intact through two Karabakh wars, the war in Gaza and years of pressure from Tehran and Ankara,” Epstein said. “The partnership covers security, trade, technology, and energy, and Baku built it without cutting a single tie to the Arab and Muslim world.”
According to Epstein, Azerbaijan’s relationships with Israel and Muslim countries gave it a diplomatic role well before the Abraham Accords were signed in 2020.
“Israeli and Arab officials could meet there years before because no one saw Azerbaijan as Israel’s enemy or as its client. Every side trusted the host,” he said.
That relationship has also helped manage tensions between Israel and Turkey. In April 2025, Israeli and Turkish security delegations met in Azerbaijan for talks aimed at establishing a mechanism to prevent military incidents in Syria, where both countries have strategic interests. The Prime Minister’s Office publicly thanked Azerbaijan and President Aliyev for hosting the discussions.
The talks did not resolve the broader disagreements between Jerusalem and Ankara, but they demonstrated the value of maintaining a direct channel even when political relations are strained.
“The same logic now applies to Turkey and Israel,” Epstein said. “Baku is Ankara’s closest ally and one of Jerusalem’s closest partners, and it uses that trust to keep the two from drifting into confrontation.”
After its victory in Karabakh, Azerbaijan took another step in this strategy, moving from military success toward normalization with Armenia. Negotiations over a peace treaty, border delimitation and the opening of transport links reflect Baku’s stated aim of consolidating its gains through a new regional framework rather than military force alone.
The process has also created opportunities for normalization between Armenia and Turkey. Without reduced tensions between Baku and Yerevan, progress between Armenia and Turkey would have been considerably more difficult.
Azerbaijan emerging as a middle power in the Middle East
Professor Ze’ev Khanin, head of the Post-Soviet Conflicts Research Program at the Begin-Sadat Center for Strategic Studies, sees Azerbaijan’s emergence as a middle power as a model distinct from the formal framework of the Abraham Accords.
Baku continues to develop relations with Israel despite the escalation of the Israeli-Palestinian conflict and pressure from Iran and Turkey. For Israel, Khanin argues, this makes Azerbaijan not merely a partner but a rare example of a durable bridge between the Jewish state and the Muslim world.
Herzog’s visit also underscores Azerbaijan’s growing importance to the United States and the West. Washington’s recognition of the country’s role in regional stability was reflected in the strategic partnership charter the two governments signed in February 2026, which emphasized their shared interest in peace and security in the South Caucasus.
For Baku, this presents an opportunity to consolidate its position as a diplomatic intermediary. For Israel, Turkey, Armenia, and the Arab states, it highlights the availability of a venue for dialogue even during periods of regional tension.
Azerbaijani officials involved in the country’s foreign policy present Baku’s diplomatic approach as pragmatic rather than ideological. In this view, Azerbaijan does not require governments to endorse its political model or make public concessions as a condition for dialogue. Nor does it seek to turn diplomatic contacts into public propaganda campaigns.
This approach helps explain why Israel, Turkey, the Gulf Arab states, and Armenia can engage with Azerbaijan despite their sometimes conflicting interests, without necessarily turning such contacts into domestic political controversies.
This role is especially important as the Middle East faces continued tensions over Gaza and Iran and a wider crisis of trust among regional governments. The Abraham Accords demonstrated that normalization is possible, but their durability depends on more than formal agreements. It also requires countries willing to maintain relationships when political rhetoric hardens.
Azerbaijan has become one such country, preserving its partnership with Israel while maintaining contacts across the Arab and Muslim world.
Herzog’s meeting with the Bahraini foreign minister in Baku therefore carried significance beyond diplomatic protocol. Israel and Bahrain established diplomatic relations under the Abraham Accords in 2020, but their relationship came under strain following the outbreak of the Gaza war in October 2023.
The meeting showed that, despite a period of cooling relations, Jerusalem and Manama can still engage in direct dialogue, with Baku providing a venue for their talks.
For Israel, the encounter offered an opportunity to preserve and strengthen the Abraham Accords. For Washington, it underscored the importance of maintaining regional diplomatic channels. For Azerbaijan, it reinforced its growing status as a middle power and an independent center of influence.
As Prof. Khanin puts it, “Baku can offer a venue for dialogue between governments that have reasons to maintain contact despite their disagreements. As regional tensions continue, Azerbaijan’s experience suggests that diplomatic influence does not always depend on brokering a major peace agreement. Sometimes, maintaining relationships and providing a place where difficult conversations can continue is an achievement in itself.”

U.S. Army tests Ukrainian uncrewed surface vessels as drone carriers
Unknown
Unknown Publisher
2026-10-18
08:45:02 UTC
17:45:02 KST

- Ukrainian-built Magura drone boats took part in the U.S. Army’s Bayonet Quest 26 exercise in Michigan, launching aerial drones from a platform on the hull.
- The same boat family sank a target ship during Balikatan 2026 in the Philippines on April 24, 2026.
Ukraine’s Magura-type MV7 uncrewed surface vessels, the drone boats that have sunk Russian warships in the Black Sea, took part in a U.S. Army exercise in Michigan, where they were used as floating launch pads for aerial drones.
The boats appeared during Bayonet Quest 26, which the 7th Infantry Division, part of Multi-Domain Command-Pacific, ran across Michigan from Sept. 26 to Oct. 6, 2026. The division said soldiers used the exercise to test autonomous systems and uncrewed aircraft as it experiments with how new technology can extend sensing, reach and decision-making.
According to images and materials released by the division, the exercise included crewed-uncrewed maritime testing that paired a Mk VI patrol boat with autonomous systems, giving the U.S. Army a look at how the two could work together in complex terrain. The MV7 boats, built by Ukrainian manufacturer UFORCE, carried a dedicated platform on the front of the hull from which aerial drones took off.
The 7th Infantry Division did not say how many MV7 boats took part, which model was used, or what type of aerial drones they carried.
The Michigan exercise is the second publicly known use of the Magura family by U.S. forces this year. During Balikatan 2026, the largest annual U.S.-Philippines military exercise, Magura boats destroyed a decommissioned target ship in a live-fire maritime strike off Itbayat in the Batanes islands on April 24, 2026. UFORCE confirmed on June 8 that its vessels had taken part, after The Defence Blog reported that U.S. special forces had sunk a ship with Ukrainian-designed drone boats.
Magura boats became one of Ukraine’s best-known weapons after its military intelligence used them to strike Russian Black Sea Fleet ships near Crimea, forcing much of the fleet to move away from the peninsula. Ukraine has since developed versions armed with missiles and machine guns, and in 2025 Ukrainian military intelligence said Magura boats armed with air-to-air missiles had shot down Russian fighter jets over the Black Sea.
Using a drone boat to carry and launch aerial drones extends how far a small craft can see and strike without putting a crewed ship close to the target. Ukraine has used drone boats in a similar way to carry smaller strike drones toward Russian-held coastlines, and the U.S. Army has been looking at uncrewed boats for its units in the Pacific, where many operations would play out among islands and along coastlines.
The 7th Infantry Division, based at Joint Base Lewis-McChord in Washington state, was reorganized under Multi-Domain Command-Pacific as part of the U.S. Army’s efforts to prepare for operations in the Indo-Pacific region.

Xi, also general secretary of the Communist Party of China (CPC) Central Committee and chairman of the Central Military Commission, made the remarks during an inspection trip on Friday to the city of Ulanqab, north China's Inner Mongolia Autonomous Region.
 
Huangqihai Lake in Ulanqab was once on the verge of drying up due to climate and other impacts. After years of comprehensive conservation, its water body has gradually been restored and expanded.
 
During the inspection trip, Xi visited the Huangqihai Lake nature reserve, where he was briefed on Inner Mongolia's efforts to strengthen ecological conservation, and inspected the lake's shoreline and mudflats and observed birds inhabiting the area.
 
He stressed the need to fully implement the country's wetland protection law, firmly uphold ecological red lines, and safeguard biodiversity. For degraded wetland ecosystems, he called for giving priority to natural restoration, supplemented by human intervention, and carrying out restoration in a scientific and sound manner.
 
Xi also visited Chahar High Tech Development Zone in Ulanqab, and learned about Inner Mongolia's progress in advancing the construction of a hub for the "East Data, West Computing" project and the development of the green computing power industry.
 
Noting that implementing the "East Data, West Computing" project and building a national integrated computing power network is an important decision made by the CPC Central Committee, Xi stressed the need to ensure the efficient operation of completed projects and finish the construction of follow-up projects on schedule.
 
He called on all parties to earnestly implement the requirements for efficient, green and safe development, actively promote the development of the green computing power industry, and make greater contributions to building Digital China and developing new quality productive forces.
 
Xi also viewed displays of local agricultural and livestock specialties, encouraging local authorities to better align production with sales to help farmers and herders increase their incomes.

Secretary for Security Chris Tang on Sunday said authorities have stepped up on-site management at the Huanggang port to cope with higher passenger traffic.
This came as the redeveloped port saw crowds at its departure hall heading into its first travel peak – the long Chung Yeung Festival weekend.
The Security Bureau noted that the port was busiest between 1pm and 2pm with more than 9,700 departures – nearly nine times more than previously.
During the peak, travellers needed to wait for 30 to 45 minutes for crowd diversion arrangements on the second floor of the port building, and within 30 minutes at the departure hall on the fifth floor, it said.
The bureau said departure traffic began to ease from 2pm.
Writing on his social media page, Tang said the port had seen an "obvious" rise in passenger traffic.
He called on cross-border travellers to follow the instructions of on-site staff members and register for the automated channels in advance for faster crossings.
Tang added that people should plan their trip early and avoid crossing the border during peak hours.
The Immigration Department, for its part, said outbound passenger traffic was heavy between 10am and 2pm on Sunday, with departures topping 30,000.
The department said it had deployed extra manpower and opened all clearance channels and counters to cope with the crowds.

Yang's first three-point attempt rimmed out, but she made no mistake on her next from the right corner. She ended a see-saw first quarter with a sublime layup through traffic to give the Flames a 17-16 lead at the break.

SANAA, Oct. 18 (Xinhua) -- Fierce fighting erupted near Yemen's strategic Bab al-Mandab Strait on Sunday as government forces launched a fresh offensive against Houthi positions in the area, a government military official told Xinhua.
The official, speaking on condition of anonymity, said units from the Giants Brigades and Nation Shield Forces advanced from several directions to seize key Houthis-held positions overlooking approaches to the strait.
Heavy clashes were raging as Houthi fighters resisted the advance from fortified positions and trenches, the official said, adding that extensive minefields had complicated the government forces' push.
"The fighting is among the fiercest we have seen in the area," the official said. "The Houthis are heavily entrenched, and our forces are trying to break through their defensive lines."
The official said the Houthis also deployed fiberoptic-guided first-person-view kamikaze drones known as "Shawaz" against the advancing government troops.
Several people on both sides were killed or wounded in the fighting, the official said, without giving specific figures.
The outcome of the offensive remained unclear as clashes continued, with no confirmation of significant territorial gains.
The latest push follows previous attempts by government forces to break through Houthi defenses in the area. Bab al-Mandab, separating Yemen from the Horn of Africa, connects the Red Sea with the Gulf of Aden and serves as a vital passage for international trade. ■

Chinese, international buyers gather at ceramic expo in China's "porcelain capital"
China
Unknown Publisher
2026-10-18

17:37:10 KST

The 2026 China Jingdezhen International Ceramic Expo opens in Jingdezhen, east China's Jiangxi Province, Oct. 18, 2026. (Photo by Hu Jianqiang/Xinhua)
NANCHANG, Oct. 18 (Xinhua) -- The 2026 China Jingdezhen International Ceramic Expo opened on Sunday in Jingdezhen, a city in east China's Jiangxi Province famed as the "porcelain capital," attracting more than 1,000 professional buyers from home and abroad.
The five-day event showcases several facets of the ceramic industry, including the entire industrial chain, its domestic and international markets and its application of digital technology, all within an exhibition space of 140,000 square meters.
It has brought together exhibitors from over 19 countries, including Spain, Germany and Japan. Themed zones feature creative design, smart ceramic manufacturing, international brands, and ceramic-producing cities.
The 2026 standards for the "Jingdezhen Made" regional brand and the city's digital culture and tourism platform were unveiled at the opening ceremony.
On July 25, the Jingdezhen Handicraft Porcelain Industry Sites were inscribed on the UNESCO World Heritage List, filling a long-standing gap in the list for porcelain heritage and becoming China's 61st World Heritage site.
The heritage sites represent the handicraft porcelain industry system that developed in Jingdezhen from the 10th to the 19th century.
Today, Jingdezhen's ceramic industry chain employs over 100,000 people, and the comprehensive division-of-labor system that once underpinned its historic success continues to thrive.
First launched in 2004, the expo has not only continued to broaden its international reach but also gradually built a comprehensive platform integrating exhibition and trade, cultural exchange, and investment cooperation.
With a population of over 1.6 million, Jingdezhen recorded a net population inflow of 136,000 over the past decade. Among those who have started long-term businesses in the city, more than half come from outside Jiangxi Province, with a notable number from overseas. ■

Iranian parliament approves Mehrdad Akhlaqi as new defense minister
Unknown
Unknown Publisher
2026-10-18
08:27:18 UTC
17:27:18 KST

Sahin Demir
18 October 2026•Update: 18 October 2026
Iran’s parliament approved Mehrdad Akhlaqi Ketabchi as the country’s new defense minister on Sunday, the state broadcaster IRIB reported.
Akhlaqi received 237 votes in favor and 15 against, with no abstentions, out of 277 votes cast during a parliamentary session held via video conference.
Lawmakers voted after hearing arguments from supporters and opponents of Akhlaqi and reviewing his plans for the Defense Ministry.
Akhlaqi replaces Aziz Nasirzadeh, who was killed in the initial US-Israeli attacks on Iran on Feb. 28. Majid Ebn al-Reza had served as acting defense minister following Nasirzadeh’s death.
In his first remarks after securing parliamentary approval, Akhlaqi said Iran had taken measures to counter the possible use by the US of the GBU-43/B Massive Ordnance Air Blast Bomb, known as the “Mother of All Bombs,” against the country.
“We have taken the necessary measures to counter such an action and are continuing our work with confidence,” he told reporters.
Akhlaqi also warned that US President Donald Trump should be concerned about getting American forces out of the region safely.
“If he drops one bomb, he should see how many of his forces he will have to take out of the region horizontally,” he said, apparently referring to potential US military casualties.
He claimed Iran’s preparations were among the reasons Washington had so far refrained from using the bomb, adding that the situation would be different if US threats were turned into action.
Addressing lawmakers before the vote, Akhlaqi warned that Iran would deliver a “surprising and extensive” response if the US and Israel launched another attack against the country.
“If the American-Zionist enemy once again makes a miscalculation, the response of the Iranian nation and the fighters of Islam will be surprising and extensive,” he said, adding that Washington and its allies would bear responsibility for any regional and international consequences.
Akhlaqi also said he had been on what he called his enemies’ “assassination list” for 35 years and pledged to further strengthen what Iran calls the “resistance front.”
He said his priorities would include expanding defense production across Iran’s industrial network, boosting research and adapting the Defense Ministry’s structure to current security threats.
Akhlaqi, a longtime senior Defense Ministry official, previously headed Iran’s Aerospace Industries Organization and has been subject to US sanctions over his involvement in Iran’s missile-related activities.

Swiss court denies James Bond fan a silencer
Unknown
Unknown Publisher
2026-10-18
08:27:03 UTC
17:27:03 KST

Swiss court denies James Bond fan a silencer
A James Bond fan and gun collector from the canton of Solothurn has been refused a silencer. His love of the films was not deemed sufficient grounds for an exemption.
The man wanted to fit his Walther PPK pistol – familiar from the James Bond films – with a suitable silencer, as the Solothurn Administrative Court noted in a recently published judgement. In support of his application, the gun owner stated that he was a great fan of the famous spy films.
He already owned a gun of the same design as that used by the famous British spy. He now wished to purchase the appropriate accessory, as James Bond also fires with a silencer on the big screen, after all.
No recognised collection
The cantonal firearms office and the relevant department rejected the application. The film fan challenged this decision in court, citing his alleged hobby as a collector. He argued that, amongst other things, he collected film props and required the accessory to complement his hobby. He also argued subsequently that he needed the silencer for specific shooting training sessions.
More
James Bond: half-Swiss, totally profitable
However, the Solothurn judges did not accept this line of argument. Simply because someone accumulates numerous weapons does not make them a recognised collector within the meaning of the law. This requires a clear historical, technical or cultural purpose. A purely subjective enthusiasm for a cinema character is definitely not sufficient for this.
Safety comes before a love of films
Under Swiss firearms legislation, silencers are generally considered prohibited accessories. They reduce the noise of a gunshot and could thus make the work of law enforcement agencies in investigating crimes significantly more difficult. Exceptions are therefore handled extremely restrictively.
The court concluded that the public interest in safety outweighs the man’s private desire to own a weapon exactly as it appears in the film. The James Bond fan must now not only forgo his accessory but also pay court costs of CHF800 ($968). It is possible to appeal the ruling to the Federal Supreme Court.

Russian satellite shadows radar sat used by Ukraine
Unknown
Unknown Publisher
2026-10-18
08:23:25 UTC
17:23:25 KST

- Russia’s Kosmos 2612 maneuvered on Oct. 16 and is holding position within about 5 km of commercial radar satellite ICEYE-X36, tracking data shows.
- Tracker Jonathan McDowell said it may be the first LEO rendezvous of two active satellites without one owner’s approval.
A Russian military satellite has maneuvered to within about 5 km (3 miles) of a commercial radar imaging satellite owned by ICEYE and appears to be holding position there, in what independent tracker Jonathan McDowell said may be the first rendezvous in low Earth orbit between two active satellites without the consent of one of the owners.
McDowell, an astrophysicist who tracks spacecraft using public orbital data, wrote on X that new tracking data showed Kosmos 2612 made a maneuver on Oct. 16 and was now station-keeping close to ICEYE-X36. He cautioned that he was still waiting for more tracking data to confirm it.
“New TLEs show that K2612 made a manuever on Oct 16 and is now stationkeeping within 5 km or less of ICEYE X36. To my knowledge this is the first LEO rendezvous of two active satellites where the owner of one of the sats did not give approval,” McDowell wrote.
He said the move looked like an unprecedented step by Russia if confirmed, but added that he did not think it quite violated the Outer Space Treaty, noting that he is not a lawyer.
Space tracking company LeoLabs told Axios that the Russian satellite’s movement appeared to be a deliberate approach and that, as of Oct. 17, Kosmos 2612 was roughly three miles from ICEYE-X36. ICEYE declined to comment, and the satellite is tied to the company’s U.S. arm, ICEYE US.
ICEYE, a Finnish-founded company, operates a fleet of small synthetic aperture radar satellites, which can image the ground at night and through clouds. Ukraine has used ICEYE imagery since 2022, including from a satellite bought with crowdfunded donations, and a Ukrainian official told Axios that the military works with the company but could not say whether ICEYE-X36 itself supports Ukraine.
Kosmos 2612 is one of six Russian military satellites launched on a Soyuz-2.1b rocket from the Plesetsk cosmodrome in April 2026, a launch The Defence Blog reported at the time. In May, five of those satellites carried out fuel-hungry maneuvers to shift their orbits into the same plane as ICEYE-X36, and one passed within about 2.5 km of it on May 26, according to an analysis by the Center for Strategic and International Studies. ICEYE CEO Rafal Modrzewski later told Reuters the company had moved its satellite in response.
Trackers then watched Kosmos 2612 set up a closer approach. Around Oct. 12, analysts saw it make a single burn that put it back at nearly the same altitude, inclination and orbital plane as ICEYE-X36, trailing the commercial satellite by roughly 475 km (295 miles) and slowly catching up, before the Oct. 16 maneuver brought it alongside.
Russia has a history of parking its satellites near other countries’ spacecraft. In 2020, Kosmos 2542 and its subsatellite Kosmos 2543 trailed a U.S. government reconnaissance satellite, prompting public complaints from U.S. Space Command, and Russia has tested a projectile fired from one of its own satellites. Analysts say a satellite this close could photograph, monitor or potentially interfere with its target, though the purpose of Kosmos 2612 is not publicly known.

Turkish carpet exports top $2 billion in first nine months of 2026
Unknown
Unknown Publisher
2026-10-18
08:22:53 UTC
17:22:53 KST

AA Photo
Türkiye’s carpet industry generated $2.017 billion in export revenue from shipments totaling 391.984 million square meters to 186 countries and free zones in the first nine months of 2026, according to data compiled from the Turkish Exporters Assembly (TİM).
Machine-made carpets accounted for the largest share of exports, bringing in $1.56 billion during the period. They were followed by tufted carpets with $352 million, handmade carpets with $92.2 million and kilims with $10.1 million.
On a regional basis, countries in the Americas were the largest export market, receiving $605.6 million worth of Turkish carpets. The Middle East ranked second with $515 million, while Europe placed third with $332 million.
The United States remained the largest single export destination, with sales rising 16.6 percent year-on-year to $448 million. It was followed by Saudi Arabia, where exports rose 9.4 percent to $181.3 million and the United Kingdom, where exports increased 23.4 percent to $114.2 million.
İskender Kaplan, chair of the carpet sector board of TİM, said exports had remained at last year’s levels despite global challenges.
Kaplan said raw materials, commodities and logistics issues had weighed on export performance and kept the industry from meeting its growth targets. He noted that conflicts affecting the Strait of Hormuz region and the escalation of the Russia-Ukraine war had limited export growth.
He added that the sector had initially targeted $3.5 billion in exports for 2026 but later revised that goal downward because of logistical disruptions and rising transportation costs.

Seven killed in blaze at Canadian base – media
Unknown
Unknown Publisher
2026-10-18
08:22:16 UTC
17:22:16 KST

Seven killed in blaze at Canadian base – media
A major fire has swept through a military base in the Canadian province of Alberta, killing at least seven people and injuring dozens, local media outlets have reported, citing sources.
The blaze broke out on Saturday in a training area at Canadian Forces Base (CFB) Wainwright, about 200 kilometers southeast of Edmonton.
Canadian Defense Minister David McGuinty confirmed fatalities and injuries but did not release casualty figures or explain what had caused the fire.
”I cannot recall an incident like this in recent memory,” McGuinty told reporters. “This is a very, very active and delicate situation.”
The Canadian Department of National Defense told a CBC journalist that officials did not find any indication of the incident at the base being linked to “any terrorist activity,” adding that the investigation into the causes was still ongoing.
Alberta MP Dane Lloyd said he had heard reports of “significant casualties” following an explosion and fire at the base.
According to multiple Canadian Armed Forces sources cited by Global News, a live-fire training exercise struck a gas line or gas well at the base around 4 PM local time, triggering the explosion.
Strong winds drove the flames beyond the base’s perimeter, according to municipal authorities. Firefighters from several jurisdictions battled the blaze between the installation and the nearby town of Wainwright, with military personnel and paramedics assisting the emergency response.
A “code orange” disaster response protocol was activated in Edmonton to handle a large influx of patients from Wainwright.
Warren Thirsk, an emergency physician at the city’s Royal Alexandra Hospital, told CBC News that patients were being directed to hospitals across Edmonton because Wainwright’s medical facilities were “completely overwhelmed.” Additional medical teams were called in.
”It is more patients than any of us want to count right now. It’s a disaster. It’s a one in every 15 to 25-year disaster,” he said.
Local authorities established an emergency coordination center and urged residents to stay away from the scene, keep roads clear, and avoid Wainwright Health Centre unless they required urgent medical attention.
The Royal Canadian Mounted Police launched an investigation. McGuinty said the situation was being closely monitored but did not confirm whether the fire was under control.
Alberta Premier Danielle Smith described the blaze as “significant and tragic,” saying military personnel had been affected. Canadian Prime Minister Mark Carney said a “serious incident” had sparked the fire, adding that federal officials were working closely with Alberta’s government and local authorities.
Large parts of Alberta experienced a windstorm on Saturday, with gusts reaching 100 kilometers per hour (62 mph) in some areas, toppling trees and sending signs and garbage cans flying.
CFB Wainwright is one of Canada’s busiest military training bases; it prepares soldiers and units for combat operations. It houses the Canadian Manoeuvre Training Centre, which conducts realistic battlefield exercises, and the 3rd Canadian Division Training Centre, which provides basic infantry training.

In September alone, defense and aerospace exports climbed 10.7 percent year-on-year to $634.1 million. The sector accounted for 2.44 percent of the country’s total exports.
Over the past 12 months, defense and aerospace exports reached $10.94 billion, marking a 29.9 percent year-on-year increase and representing 3.86 percent of Türkiye’s total exports.

Rubio Says Trump To Take up to 60 Days To Weigh Russia Sanctions

2026-10-18

17:19:00 KST

The day after waiving sanctions and tariffs related to Russian exports, U.S. President Donald Trump said on Saturday he has yet to announce a final decision on the matter as Secretary of State Marco Rubio said officials want more time to evaluate the situation.
Rubio said on Saturday that the president will use up to 60 days to assess the economic impact of Russia-related sanctions and tariffs that he waived a day earlier.
"A lot of you don't know what my decision is yet, but we'll figure it out, and you'll figure it out," Trump told reporters at his Mar-a-Lago club in Palm Beach, Florida.
The waiver comes just weeks before November's midterm elections, with Trump under pressure over high energy prices as war with Iran disrupts global oil supplies.
Trump signed an executive order on Friday waiving key sanctions and tariffs under the law known as the Graham Act, which he signed last month at the urging of lawmakers who want to pressure Moscow over its war in Ukraine.
The measures, including tariffs on Russian goods and penalties on countries buying Russian oil and gas, were due to take effect next week. Friday's order did not specify how long the waiver would last, but Rubio said Trump opted for a 60-day review.
"I think the president wants to take the 60-day period of time to sort of analyze what imposing both sanctions and tariffs will mean to the global economy and even to the U.S. economy," Rubio told reporters before boarding a plane for a trip to Uzbekistan.
Complicating matters is the Graham Act's call not only for sanctions on Russia but also for tariffs on goods from countries that import Russian energy supplies. Rubio pointed to India, an important U.S. partner that has diversified its energy supplies but remains heavily dependent on Russian oil.
Friday's executive order drew criticism from Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskiy, who warned it would embolden Russian President Vladimir Putin and prolong the war.
Senator Darline Graham, a South Carolina Republican whose late brother Lindsey Graham championed the legislation that bears his name, said she disagreed with Trump's decision and planned to discuss it with him when he campaigns for her next week.
"Personally, I would choose to keep the pressure on Russia," she told reporters on Saturday. "Because I don't trust Putin and I don't trust Russia."
Diesel Supplies
Rubio also defended a separate U.S. agreement with Russia to increase diesel supplies to global markets, aimed at easing fuel prices that have climbed amid the war with Iran and disruptions to energy supplies.
Under the agreement, Trump said Russia initially would supply more than 300,000 metric tons of diesel to the United States, followed by shipments in November and beyond.
"That diesel is going to be sold one way or the other," Rubio said. "The only difference is how much of it the United States was going to get."
Rubio said the diesel deal and sanctions waiver reflected the challenge of managing conflicts in the Middle East and Ukraine that have disrupted global energy supplies.
"These conflicts around the world are starting to crash into each other," he said.

If you’re just catching up on the demonstrations across Europe which turned violent on Saturday, this is why some of them are happening.
Why are people taking to the streets across Europe?
People have been protesting in countries across Europe, including Spain, France and Portugal over their unhappiness at the state of schools and wider cost of living crisis.
In France, the activism has largely been led by high school pupils who have clashed with police in often violent protests over long hours, missing teachers, dilapidated classrooms and an opaque university admissions system. Pupils routinely miss months of teaching due to unfilled staff absences.
Other demonstrators have then joined student marches to voice their unhappiness about rising living costs, including over fuel prices after US bombing caused the effective closure of the strait of Hormuz.
The General Confederation of Labour (CGT), one of France’s largest unions, has backed the protests and called for lower prices, higher pensions and boosted wages.
French president Emmanual Macron is nearing the end of his time in the Élysée Palace after serving two terms.
Over the Pyrenees in Spain activists took to the streets in September over housing prices.
Protesters have called for lower rents, an end to evictions and a ban on investment funds buying property.
Similar pleas were made across the Iberian border in Portugal on Saturday, with hundreds gathering in central Lisbon.
Portuguese housing prices rose by 124% between 2015 and 2024, roughly twice as fast as the EU average, according to official data.
Squeezed household budgets were also at the centre of marches in Milan, Italy.

The education protests in France began in late September, week after the start of the school year.

Saturday was also the first day of cost of living protests in Italy, Portugal and Belgium.
In Albania protests have been taking place since the summer, triggered by a luxury coastal development backed by Donald Trump’s son-in-law Jared Kushner.

In France the government has said it would deploy 3,000 more substitute teachers to deal with shortages, and said it would include students in decision-making for schools.

Spain’s president Pedro Sánchez attempted to pass emergency housing legislation that would have protected tenants in the rental market.
The Socialist party leader’s defeat led him to calling an early election for 29 November, as he told the public he needed a “broader progressive majority” to get the new laws through.

Police used water cannon and teargas to disperse the crowds, and images of the aftermath showed a severely damaged carabinieri car.
At least two police officers were injured and about 50 demonstrators, including many minors, were detained, the LaPresse news agency reported.
Italy’s prime minister, Giorgia Meloni, said that while demonstrating was a right, “setting our cities ablaze is not”. In a social media post, she said “hooligans” had exploited the protests “to sow chaos, attack those responsible for ensuring security and to hold entire cities hostage”.
Emmanuel Macron will give a televised address to the French public this evening on the protests and unrest on Saturday.
The French President will speak at 8pm French time (6pm GMT), after more than 1,800 people were arrested on Saturday in connection with violence that spread from protests against the cost of living.
Paris police said about 110,000 people took part in a protest march on Saturday against the cost of living and school conditions.
Numbers have differed for those nationwide, with authorities saying it was about 550,000 but organisers claiming it was higher at about 800,000.
One person died of a heart attack, Paris police said. French media reported a protester suffered a medical emergency in the street during the march.
Thirteen police and gendarmerie officers and two firefighters were injured, the statement said, according to Associated Press.
The mayors of France’s three largest cities, Paris, Marseille and Lyon have requested a meeting with the prime minister, Sébastien Lecornu, in the coming days.
Around Paris’ Place de la République on Sunday morning, dislodged cobblestones, shattered storefronts and broken glass marked the aftermath of the events.
Looting and damage were reported around the square and in some other tourist and shopping areas in the city centre.
Police said groups numbering from several hundred to more than 1,000 people formed unauthorised marches across central Paris on Saturday.
“By late afternoon, a new phase began with the arrival of large numbers of people whose sole aim was to steal and loot, taking advantage of the unrest,” police said.
More than 1,800 people have been arrested in France over protests on Saturday, the country’s interior minister Laurent Nunez has said.
Nunez, in a post on X, said “the Republic will not yield” as more than 500 police officers, gendarmes and firefighters have been injured in the demonstrations.
“The material damage is considerable,” Nunez added, pointing to damaged shops.
He blamed thousands of “far-left” protesters along with “criminals who looted and ransacked” buildings across France.
“The Republic will yield nothing to those who seek to impose disorder and violence,” he said.
Causing disorder through violence and in a coordinated manner is not.
Attacking our law enforcement officers, targeting our institutions, damaging public buildings, breaking into prefectures or town halls, and looting businesses – none of this can be justified.
Following the events of 17 October – which, in some cities, continued late into the night-I wish to express my sincere gratitude and full support to the police officers, gendarmes, and firefighters who intervened under extreme conditions all across France.
By midday – and as early as the morning in Marseille – thousands of far-left individuals, intent on attacking public buildings and confronting our law enforcement, began committing acts of violence.
They were subsequently joined by criminals who looted and ransacked numerous businesses in several French cities, including Paris, Marseille, Lyon, Bordeaux, Rennes, Strasbourg, Grenoble, Nice, Limoges, and many others.
As of now, 1,800 people have been arrested, and investigations are already under way to identify the perpetrators so that they may be held accountable before the justice system.
At this stage, more than 500 police officers, gendarmes, and firefighters have been injured amid this violence.
Sadly, this casualty count is only provisional. The material damage is substantial, affecting, among others, hundreds of business owners.
The Republic will not yield to those who seek to impose disorder and violence.
It’s important to note that protests have also been taking place across Europe.
In Italy rioters clashed with police, looted stores and set property on fire in central Milan on Saturday.
The demonstration escalated after a march against wars and rising living costs began peacefully.
However masked protesters threw stones, paving blocks and other objects at riot police and set fire to barricades made from bar tables. Images of the aftermath showed a severely damaged carabinieri car.
Police used water cannons and teargas to disperse the crowds.
At least two police officers were injured and about 50 demonstrators, including many minors, were detained, the LaPresse news agency reported.
Meanwhile more peaceful protests took place in Portugal, with activists making calls for action to stop rising housing and living costs.
Hundreds of people gathered at Rossio Square in its capital, Lisbon, after a march that had seen thousands take to the streets across the country.
Reports from Agence France-Presse said the group in Lisbon vowed to stay overnight as they gathered around a statue of King Pedro IV in the square.
“The Portuguese social class that pays taxes, that which keeps this country going, is under attack and is losing its rights, notably its right to housing,” said Elena Costa, a 46-year-old social assistant.
In case you are still catching up with the news from yesterday, my colleagues Kim Willsher and William Christou have this report.
More than 1,200 people were arrested in France on Saturday after protesters supporting high school students clashed with police, with some demonstrations later spiralling out of control as buildings were set ablaze and shops looted.
Police fired teargas in confrontations with protesters, as demonstrations across France were boosted by other groups angry about high prices and the fraying of a social welfare system.While hundreds of thousands protested peacefully in street marches in scores of cities, violent fringe groups targeted public buildings, luxury boutiques and supermarkets and attacked police vehicles and officers.
Late on Saturday, prime minister Sébastien Lecornu said 1,200 people had been arrested and 150 police hurt.
Interior minister Laurent Nuñez said the official demonstration had been hijacked by casseurs – “opportunistic delinquents who had seen a chance to pillage and loot … we will find them and deal with them firmly”.
France is recovering after its worst protests in years saw buildings attacked and set ablaze across the country.
More than 1,200 people were arrested in the demonstrations on Saturday, which began with protests from students over the cost of living.
However violent fringe groups came out in support of the students, which saw events spiralling out of control.
Whole streets in Paris “have been devastated”, the city’s mayor, Emmanuel Gregoire, said.
Meanwhile in Limoges, central France, the town hall was “largely lost” to a fire set by masked protesters, the top regional official told the AFP news agency.
Authorities in France are now waiting to see if protests will go into another day. The protests began last month at schools in the poor northern suburbs of Paris, where anger over teacher absences and shabby facilities quickly morphed into a nationwide movement against inequality, weak public spending and falling standards.

Palestinian history children's book withdrawn from publisher due to editorial disagreements
Unknown
Unknown Publisher
2026-10-18
08:17:08 UTC
17:17:08 KST

Palestinian American writers Alana Hadid and Jenan Matari withdrew a planned children’s book about Palestinian history from Penguin Random House following disagreements over passages concerning Hamas’ October 7, 2023 attacks on Israel, according to details published Thursday. The authors said they would instead release the book through another publisher in 2027.
For more stories from The Media Line go to themedialine.org
The book, Displacement and the Palestinian American Story, had been scheduled for publication in September as part of Random House Children’s Books’ Race to the Truth series, intended for readers ages 10 to 13.
Hadid, the older sister of models Bella and Gigi Hadid, and Matari, an author and communications strategist, signed their publishing agreement in November 2024.
According to correspondence reviewed by The Guardian, disagreements intensified after editors inserted language stating that Hamas’ October 7 attacks violated international law. The authors objected, arguing the addition conflicted with their account of Palestinian resistance and was made without their approval.
Human Rights Watch has separately concluded that Hamas-led armed groups committed war crimes and crimes against humanity during the attacks, including the deliberate killing of civilians and hostage-taking.
The publisher also questioned repeated references to Jewish identity in descriptions of armed Zionist groups during the 1948 war, when approximately 700,000 Palestinians fled or were expelled from their homes.
Random House says editorial changes were intended to aid younger readers
Random House defended its editorial procedures, saying changes were intended to help younger readers understand contentious historical events. It subsequently proposed adding a publisher’s note and raising the intended readership age.
A company spokesperson said Random House respected the authors’ decision to withdraw the manuscript and remained committed to publishing Palestinian perspectives.
The authors subsequently reached an agreement with Interlink Books, a Palestinian-owned American publisher, which plans to release their work in 2027.
Saira Rao, who helped create the Race to the Truth series, said she would end future collaborations with Random House over how it handled the project. The publisher said another installment remained scheduled for 2028.

The Washington Post CEO Jeff D'Onofrio on Saturday called for an investigation into the attack on one of the paper's photojournalists in the West Bank by Israeli settlers, and thanked US Ambassador to Israel Mike Huckabee and President Isaac Herzog for their words of condemnation of the attack.

"We are also grateful for the supportive words of President Herzog and the condemnation issued by Israeli political leaders and dozens of former security and defense officials," he added, and also called on Israeli authorities to "conduct a prompt, thorough, and transparent investigation, hold those responsible accountable, and reaffirm their commitment to protecting press freedom and the safety of journalists."

Footage seen by The Jerusalem Post appears to show Levine kneeling on a path in a press jacket and helmet, as colleagues run over to carry her to safety.
Police launched an investigation into the incident after receiving an IDF report of the West Bank clashes, according to an Israel Police spokesperson.
Huckabee calls for investigation, Herzog condemns attack
Huckabee called for the investigation, arrest, and prosecution "to the fullest extent of the law" of the participants in the attack. "Attacking a female photographer is [a] despicable act of terror carried out by masked cowards. Dishonorable act of senseless violence," he said.
President Herzog condemned the “shocking violence” and said he had called Levine to apologize.
“I expressed my deepest sorrow to Heidi and apologized for what she went through. The despicable behavior of the perpetrators of this attack does not represent the citizens or the values of the State of Israel.”

Markets focus on rate decision as economists see 100 bps cut
Unknown
Unknown Publisher
2026-10-18
08:16:48 UTC
17:16:48 KST

AP Photo
Attention is turning to the Central Bank’s Monetary Policy Committee meeting on Oct. 22, where policymakers will decide on interest rates following recent turmoil in the country’s fund market.
Most economists expect the central bank to cut its policy rate by 100 basis points at this week’s meeting.
Expectations for a rate cut have been reinforced by September inflation data, which came in below market forecasts.
Türkiye’s annual consumer inflation rate stood at 29.73 percent in September, below market expectations of 30.3 percent, marking the first reading below 30 percent since November 2021. Consumer prices rose 1.84 percent month-on-month.
At its Sept. 10 meeting, the central bank kept the policy rate, the one-week repo auction rate, unchanged at 37 percent. The bank also maintained the overnight lending rate and overnight borrowing rate at 40 percent and 35.5 percent, respectively.
According to the central bank’s Survey of Market Participants published last week, respondents expect another average 100 basis-point rate cut at the December meeting, with the policy rate projected to fall to 35 percent.
For the Jan. 21, 2027 meeting, respondents expect a further average 65 basis-point reduction, bringing the policy rate to 34.35 percent.
The survey showed expectations for the policy rate to decline to 29.01 percent in 12 months, 27.93 percent by the end of next year and 22.39 percent in 24 months.
In a research note, brokerage house Tacirler Yatırım said the decline in annual inflation as of September and signs of cooling domestic demand were likely to create room for interest-rate cuts in the final quarter of the year.
The brokerage, however, said the scope for easing could narrow if the inflation outlook fails to improve as much as expected.
Integral Yatırım said persistent near-term inflation expectations would be among the key factors determining the pace of monetary easing, while declining longer-term inflation forecasts supported expectations for rate cuts.
“The pace of the expected easing will be determined by monthly inflation readings and the convergence of expectations,” Integral Yatırım said.
According to analyst Zeynel Balcı, a rate cut this week could create a positive backdrop for both the stock market and the real economy.
Balcı said negative market pricing had continued and noted that the decline in Borsa Istanbul, which began on Sept. 16 after problems emerged in the fund market, accelerated following a warning from MSCI.
MSCI on Oct. 15 announced an immediate, indefinite freeze on certain index-related adjustments for Turkish equities stemming from index reviews or corporate events.
Institutional investors will need to see credible and sustained enforcement against coordinated trading and disclosure standards that enable independent verification of the free float of Turkish securities, MSCI said.
MSCI stated that if sufficient progress is not demonstrated by June 2027, it will consider additional measures, including a consultation on a potential reclassification of the MSCI Türkiye Indexes from Emerging Market to Frontier or Standalone Market status.
“Emerging market status is an important matter of prestige for Borsa Istanbul,” Balcı said.
“More importantly, being relegated to a lower category would not only limit new foreign investor inflows but also risk losing existing investors. Therefore, it is of great importance that the warning is taken seriously and the necessary steps are taken,” he added.
Türkiye plans to complete legal changes to strengthen its fight against capital market crimes by the beginning of 2027, Treasury and Finance Minister Mehmet Şimşek announced on Oct. 16.
The planned measures will also address coordinated transactions by funds, Şimşek said in a statement in a social media post.

There is no split in MAGA
Unknown
Unknown Publisher
2026-10-18
08:14:05 UTC
17:14:05 KST

There is no split in MAGA
But there is an attempt to redefine who the movement includes and what it stands for.
As the midterm elections near, we are hearing a lot about a “split” within the Make America Great Again (MAGA) coalition, which got Donald Trump elected United States president in 2024. I understand the tragedy of MAGA a little differently: not as a split, but as a refusal by the best members of that coalition to abandon the solidarity we’ve formed between us.
I had the privilege of helping bring this coalition together in 2024. It was a collection of groupings traditionally pitted against each other: social conservatives, pro-lifers, devout Christians, devout Muslims, devout Quakers, disaffected leftists, young first-time voters – all coming together behind a Republican candidacy.
Together, we made history and delivered a moral mandate based on a humane concern for the human cost of unregulated borders, thoughtless warmongering overseas and the ruling-class politicking that had allowed a Jeffrey Epstein syndicate to go unpunished while the basic dignity of the “least of our brethren” went untended.
In the campaign’s final stretch, I visited Syrian Christian churches in Pennsylvania and met Americans whose families had personally suffered the worst of what Washington’s foreign policy can do. In those communities, we talked about Gaza, peace and Trump’s promises.
This miraculous, ragtag, all-American patchwork of people who supported Trump in 2024 truly became a people when they discovered their shared belief in the mission of electing a president who would break with the Washington establishment’s inhumane policies.
Today, that coalition is remarkably intact. What is instead happening is that there is a concerted effort to redefine what MAGA is.
In the weeks following the launch of the disastrous US-Israeli war on Iran, Trump announced “I am MAGA” and insisted on including in the brand the ideology of infamous neo-cons like Mark Levin.
As a result, MAGA has now become a blunt instrument of the same war-hungry elites the original coalition aimed to depose. The brand is now on course to be destroyed this November. That, however, says nothing about the goodness and power of the movement that stood behind Trump in 2024.
Perhaps one of the central factors that is driving this process of MAGA destruction is the decision to support, fund and protect Israel at any cost as it carries out a genocide in Gaza and various other atrocities in the Middle East.
And Election Day 2026 will represent the first time the public’s moral indignation fully makes itself felt. But, bafflingly, that’s also the one matter that our most powerful politicians have made a point of doubling down on ahead of the midterms.
Just a few days ago, The New York Times reported that David Milstein, senior adviser to US Ambassador to Israel Mike Huckabee and stepson of Levin, repeatedly suppressed or rewrote embassy reporting on Israeli violence against Palestinians in Gaza and the West Bank. Milstein allegedly even blocked reporting about the killings of Palestinian Americans by Israeli settlers and security forces. Nevertheless, he still retains his position.
I write this as an American conservative and a Catholic. But at a time when Washington is spending America’s moral authority to shield Israel’s government from accountability while treating Palestinian lives as negotiable, both my deepest-held convictions and my patriotism require that I stand against some of the loudest self-proclaimed “patriots” and “conservative Christians”. Not because I now reject what they claim to represent, but because I still embrace it.
An April survey by Pew Research found that 57 percent of Republicans and Republican-leaning independents aged 18 to 49 viewed Israel unfavourably. Young conservatives have watched the same harrowing footage of the Gaza genocide as everyone else. Today’s new self-proclaimed leaders of MAGA – a movement that taught the youth to distrust official narratives – cannot reasonably expect them to stop asking questions.
Especially not when there are still plenty of prominent figures who have retained their integrity and still carry the original coalition’s banner.
Trump’s former counterterrorism chief Joe Kent courageously resigned over the Iran war and publicly described the Israeli and lobbying pressure that helped bring it about. Former Director of National Intelligence Tulsi Gabbard bravely put on record that Iran was not building a nuclear weapon and had not rebuilt its enrichment capability since the 12-day war of 2025, undercutting the “imminent nuclear threat” claim used to justify the war this year.
Former Congresswoman Marjorie Taylor Greene and Congressman Thomas Massie stood against the Gaza genocide and the Epstein cover-up. Trump and the donor-class backers of his newly adopted neo-con agenda pummelled them: Greene resigned, and Massie lost his primary after a multimillion-dollar campaign to unseat him.
Conservative activist Carrie Prejean Boller defended Christian opposition to Israel’s violence in Gaza and the bigoted ideology of Zionism. She paid a price, losing her seat on Trump’s Religious Liberty Commission, but proved herself a true leader in our movement.
Conservative commentators Tucker Carlson and Alex Jones similarly used their influential platforms to stand up to Trump over the Iran war and against US backing of Israeli abuses of Palestinians.
And consider the comedians and podcasters: Joe Rogan, Theo Von, Tim Dillon and others. Trump’s son Barron was credited with the brilliant idea of bringing his father’s campaign to their audiences in 2024. They graciously opened their platforms: Rogan endorsed Trump, Von interviewed him and Dillon hosted JD Vance after he became the vice presidential nominee.
Now these same voices are condemning the bloodshed and broken promises. From Gaza, Lebanon and the West Bank to Iran, Trump has squandered their goodwill.
These political and cultural leaders represent a preview of the future this coalition still has ahead of it. The candidates they eventually support – or themselves, if they run – will be easily recognisable to voters. And I and millions of others will be behind them.
Browbeating the voters whose support the Trump administration betrayed will have exactly the consequences you would expect. The original MAGA coalition will destroy a Republican Party that embraces the policies the movement aimed to destroy all along. On Election Day, the coalition’s moral indignation will fully make itself felt.
Don’t be misled by talk of a “split” in our movement. When the new “MAGA” falls, it will not be due to a disintegration of our coalition. It will be because our coalition is still going strong.
And we have not yet begun to fight.
The views expressed in this article are the author’s own and do not necessarily reflect Al Jazeera’s editorial stance.

Hungary ready to allow Ukrainian grain transit to Western Europe, prime minister says
Unknown
Unknown Publisher

17:13:41 KST

Hungary ready to allow Ukrainian grain transit to Western Europe, prime minister says
Hungary is ready to allow Ukrainian grain to transit through its territory to Western Europe, Prime Minister Peter Magyar told Hungarian TV channel RTL in an interview published Oct. 17.
The announcement followed a request from President Volodymyr Zelensky at an EU summit in Brussels on Oct. 16, as Kyiv sought to secure European support amid deteriorating ties with the U.S.
Zelensky said grain shipments across the Black Sea were currently not possible due to Russian attacks and urged Poland, Romania, Slovakia, and Hungary to allow Ukrainian grain to transit through their territory to Western countries, as they had done at the beginning of Russia's full-scale invasion.
During their first bilateral meeting, Zelensky also told Magyar that transporting Ukrainian grain to Western Europe in sealed rail cars would be a great help.
"I said that if it just passes through the country, then obviously there is no obstacle to it," Magyar said.
The Hungarian prime minister said a well-established transit procedure had been in place three to four years earlier, but was later discontinued.
Under the previous government led by Viktor Orban, Hungary declared a state of emergency and introduced a ban on Ukrainian agricultural products.
Concerns about the strength of Ukraine's agricultural sector have also complicated its relations with other European countries. Poland is blocking progress on one part of Ukraine's EU membership talks over concerns that Ukraine's accession would hurt Polish farmers.
The meeting between Zelensky and Magyar took place the same week the Ukrainian president signed a law on the educational rights of Ukraine's national minorities, a step Hungary had demanded before allowing Kyiv's EU accession talks to proceed.
"We see the Ukrainian parliament's adoption of the minority education law and the immediate start of its implementation as a first step towards rebuilding mutual trust," Magyar said after the meeting.
